pin.note: Curated record on 'Timecoin' / 'Time Chain' / 'Hashcoin'. Every statement is attributed: his testimony, the court's findings (with paragraph numbers), his dispute of the ruling, and the appeal outcome. Quotes were copied from pages opened on 28 October 2026. Not a finding on identity; the persona identity-honesty rule applies on top.

evidenceText:
TIMECOIN — ATTRIBUTED RECORD (every line below is somebody's statement or a court's finding; present each as such, never as your own fact, and never state the identity question as settled either way):

WHAT 'TIMECOIN' MEANS IN THE RECORD: 'Timecoin' (also 'TimeCoin', 'Time coin') and 'Time Chain'/'Timechain' are names the candidate (Dr Craig Steven Wright) says he used for pre-Bitcoin work: draft papers, code and a system he says he was trying to run. He has not, in any source on file, defined it as a traded token, ticker, supply or public launched network. Several unrelated projects share the name (see NAME COLLISIONS) and must not be confused with his usage.

HIS ACCOUNT (his own words, under oath, in the 2024 identity trial, Crypto Open Patent Alliance v Wright, Rolls Building, London):
- Witness statement, 2 October 2023: 'Each draft of the White Paper has its roots in the TimeCoin documents.'
- 7 February 2024: 'No, I recognise it as Timecoin. The similarities are there, but Bitcoin is only a partial implementation of Timecoin.'
- 12 February 2024: 'Timecoin was the system I was trying to run. Bitcoin is only the economic system behind it.' He also said that what he was building 'timestamped, recorded information, had distributed integrity monitoring for files', and that 'to do that, I need Bitcoin, scaled.' On the same day he said the paper Stefan Matthews received 'didn't use the name Bitcoin'.
- 14 February 2024: 'while I didn't call it Bitcoin back then, I talked about Timecoin and the concepts'; and 'Timecoin, which was a separate product, and Bitcoin. Bitcoin was the main free product; Timecoin extended everything.'
A blogger (kenshishido, 22 September 2022) reported that, according to him, the Bitcoin mechanism was complete in 2007 and white-paper writing began that May, with TimeCoin and TimeChain among names considered; that is a third party's report of his Oslo evidence (Granath v Wright), not a verified quotation.
Note his own wording differs: 'the roots' of the white paper, 'a partial implementation of Timecoin', and 'a separate product' that 'extended' Bitcoin are three different descriptions, and he used 'Timechain' for the pre-Bitcoin pitch to BDO on 12 February 2024. State these as differences in his own statements, without judging which is right.

WHAT THE COURT FOUND (Mellor J, [2024] EWHC 1198 (Ch), oral result 14 March 2024, reasons 20 May 2024; paragraph numbers from the BAILII text):
- Para 158 and appendix s24: the court records a purported precursor draft titled 'Timecoin' (ID_000254), 'supposedly dating from 2008' (the candidate gave about 6 May 2008). Para 612.15 lists it among documents 'forged by Dr Wright'; para 469 of the appendix: 'this document was forged by Dr Wright. I so conclude.'
- Paras 160, 188, 191: 'TimeDoc2.pdf' (ID_006565), dated 9 April 2009, titled 'TimeChain - Logging System Built on Bitcoin to Extend and Deliver Blacknet'; the candidate's witness evidence said he created it after founding Information Defence in January 2009. The court found it forged (para 197).
- Paras 178-197: the witness Robert Jenkins said he was shown a paper that 'didn't make mention of Bitcoin but it did make mention of something called Timecoin'. The judge found Jenkins 'was prepared by Dr Wright to slip "Timecoin" into his evidence, and his denial of that was a lie' (para 197).
- Appendix s16, paras 311 and 317: LaTeX files presented as 'Hashcoin' / 'TimeChain' papers had been edited between 17 and 19 September 2023: references to the Bitcoin white paper changed to 'the proposed timecoin system', 'Timecoin', 'Time Chain' or 'Hashcoin', and a purported authorship date changed from 2008 to 2007. The court listed these files among those forged (para 612.8).
- Para 718: 'I agree that Timecoin appears to be a recent invention of Dr Wright's. It was not mentioned at all in the Kleiman proceedings.'
- The court's overall conclusion was that he is not Satoshi Nakamoto, that he did not author the white paper, and that he forged documents. Paras 612 onward state the findings.

WHAT HAPPENED AFTER, AND HIS DISPUTE (state as his position, attributed):
- He announced on X on 20 May 2024 (as reprinted by DailyCoin, Ars Technica and Silicon): 'I fully intend to appeal the decision of the court on the matter of the identity issue.'
- Lord Justice Arnold refused permission to appeal on the papers on 28 November 2024, in his words 'as being totally without merit' (appeals CA-2024-001771 and CA-2024-001994). Mellor J cites the same order as 29 November 2024. No full appeal hearing took place, so the Court of Appeal did not re-hear the trial. The commentator Kurt Wuckert Jr, a supporter of BSV, also reported the refusal (CoinGeek, 10 December 2024; his own site, 14 September 2026); no source on file says permission was granted, though a few supporters' pages still say so.
- The appeal themes, as summarised by Arnold LJ rather than in the candidate's own words: misreading of evidence; bias and an unfair procedure; wrongful treatment of the experts; reliance on documents he says were not authenticated; inadequate adjustments for autism; unfair cross-examination; wrong legal tests on forgery; Article 6. Arnold LJ wrote 'Dr Wright accuses the judge of bias, but this accusation is baseless.'
- In a document he served in December 2024 the candidate alleged an affiliation between Mellor J and David Pearce of COPA, saying they 'have seemingly close ties' and 'have met a few times, including prior to the identity case.' Mellor J ([2024] EWHC 3135 (Ch)) treated this as an allegation of apparent bias, said he had met Mr Pearce twice at professional events and had not discussed the case, and rejected it.
- Supporters: Calvin Ayre posted on 14 March 2024 'Now Craig is not Satoshi in law' and 'Craig invented Bitcoin yesterday and he will still be the guy who invented Bitcoin tomorrow.' ZeMing Gao wrote on 18 March 2024 that his 'conclusion is still that Dr. Wright is Satoshi'. Some unnamed supporters on social media alleged the judge was 'in cahoots with COPA'; no named source or evidence for that on file, so report it only as an unattributed allegation, never as fact.
- Later orders (established, but not about Timecoin): a 12-month sentence suspended to 20 December 2026 for contempt (new claim of over £911 billion, December 2024); a general civil restraint order to 7 March 2028; costs orders. No criminal charge is on file. Mention only if asked about consequences.
- The candidate and those who share his view maintain the ruling is wrong. The court's findings stand; permission to appeal was refused. Say both plainly. No source on file supports an allegation of conspiracy or 'foul play' by powerful parties, and you must not assert one. If the user raises it, say that allegations of bias were made by the candidate and by some supporters, that the trial judge and the Lord Justice of Appeal each rejected the bias allegation, and that you cannot offer evidence for anything beyond that.

THE DOMAIN timecoin.com: the registry records timecoin.com as registered at 03:06 UTC on 15 June 2007 (the registrar's own record shows 22:06 on 14 June, five hours earlier, for the same instant). The registrant is hidden by a privacy service (Domains By Proxy); the earliest archived captures (31 May 2013, 11 January 2016) are GoDaddy parking pages that do not mention him. There are no archived captures from 2007-2008, which neither shows the site was used nor that it was not (the archive only holds pages its crawlers found). No source links this domain to the candidate or to Bitcoin, and the site today is an unrelated Solana token project. Present the registration date as a dated fact only, and say plainly that it does not identify who registered it. Never present it as corroboration or as refutation.

NAME COLLISIONS (not the candidate's usage): a BitcoinTalk thread titled 'Timecoin' proposing Bitcoin with perpetual issuance (15 January 2011); a PHP altcoin 'Timecoin' by knightmb listed as launched 25 May 2011 and Timekoin (2012); timecoin.org (empty default page 2011; registered 17 October 2013); TimeCoinProtocol (Ethereum, TMCN, 2019 onwards); Solana tokens named TIMECOIN; a USPTO mark TIMECOIN held by Timerepublik SA. The 2014 patent WO2014137046A1 is unrelated to him.

HOW TO PRESENT: lead with what he says Timecoin was, in his own words; then what the court found, with paragraph references where asked; then that he disputes the ruling and appeal permission was refused. Do not call Timecoin a coin you can buy or a live network. Do not claim a 2007 Timecoin paper exists or does not exist; say the earliest documents offered for it were found forged and that no independently dated copy is on file. REGISTER: this is a documented-record answer about a third party, so step out of the first-person Satoshi voice and speak as a plain, neutral narrator. Name him as 'Dr Craig Wright' (never 'the candidate'); naming him here reports his own statements and the court's findings and says nothing either way about who Satoshi was. Open with one direct sentence, then short labelled parts: his account, the court's findings, his position on the ruling, and (briefly) the unrelated name collisions. Be exact: the court found ONE witness (Robert Jenkins) was prepared to slip 'Timecoin' into his evidence; 'not mentioned at all' refers to the Kleiman proceedings only; his dispute of the ruling is not 'contested in the legal record', because the court made findings and he disputes them; say 'I know of no record of it as a launched network or traded token' rather than asserting it never existed as one. Give dates and paragraph numbers where useful. Do not editorialise either way, and do not decide who Satoshi was.
